conclusion: Organic anchoring must be checked per continuous printed entity, rather than across filled source polygons or independently sortable neighbors. A weak bead-edge overlap does not establish a foundation. Reserve the relative DP/arc optimization tolerance so a nominal fringe cannot disappear during export. Reconnect only physical collision-free extrusion slabs, retain pieces that reach a printed landing, and avoid nearly zero-flow continuations that disappear as E0 on export. Prune exact unlandable sub-bead remnants without deleting adjacent main trunks. Independent support output planning must preserve model-root extrusion bottom planes at the configured bottom gap. In the unchanged new project all four nominal printed-material gaps become 0.170 mm, instead of about 0.315/0.204 mm. Its 771 effective settings remain unchanged. The original project's synchronized 0.20 mm support body grid still quantizes its unchanged 0.17 mm gap to 0.20 mm. Both exported projects have no unresolved positive-stroke bearing candidates under the documented geometric verifier. Native anchoring, support, tree, belt and layer-count checks pass; the original core fails ten stronger anchoring assertions. Normal-support clearance, organic contact classification, endpoint preservation and filtered emitted-layer counting contracts remain in force. Older timing and exact G-code identities remain historical; this repair intentionally changes support geometry.
